title: Committee of Supply – Head T (Ministry of National Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head T (Ministry of National Development)

sections.label: First-timer families BTO ballot help
sections.summary: Asks HDB for details on helping first-timers with children and those starting families soon get a better chance at a BTO flat.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: With Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong outlining that more help would be given to first-timer families with children by giving them an additional ballot for their Build-To-Order (BTO) flat applications, can the Housing and Development Board (HDB) provide more details how they intend to help first-timers who plan to start their families soon after settling down and first-timers with children to achieve a better chance at securing a BTO flat?

sections.label: More larger flats, fewer 3-room
sections.summary: Proposes more 4- or 5-room or larger flats and fewer 3-room flats in new precincts for a specified housing supply period.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: First, more 4- or 5- room or larger flats and reduce 3-room flats in new precincts for a specified period of housing supply.

sections.label: Singles rent or share VERS flats
sections.summary: Proposes allowing singles to share or rent flats directly from HDB for flats undergoing the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Second, allow singles to share or rent flats that is directly from HDB for flats that will undergo Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme (VERS).

sections.label: Rent VERS flats without age limit
sections.summary: Asks why VERS flats cannot be rented or shared by singles without the age limit of 35 pegged to singles owning flats.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: If HDB plans to tear down the VERS flats in phases to free the land for different purposes, why not consider making such flats available for rental by singles or on sharing basis without having the age limit pegged to 35 years of age as that remains for singles who wish to own their flats?

sections.label: 2-room Flexi supply and Silver Bonus
sections.summary: Notes 2-room Flexi flats still mean new supply and asks the Minister whether Silver Housing Bonus take-up has been encouraging.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, 2-room Flexi flats still mean new supply must be placed in the market.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: I wish to ask Minister whether the take-up rate for the Silver Housing Bonus has been encouraging.

sections.label: HDB support for seniors and housing schemes
sections.summary: Asks HDB plans to support seniors and cites PSP's Affordable Homes Scheme and Millennial Apartments Scheme for affordable public housing.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can Minister also share what are HDB plans to better support the needs of our seniors?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Progress Singapore Party (PSP) has recommended the Affordable Homes Scheme (AHS) and the Millennial Apartments Scheme to deliver affordable and accessible public housing to Singaporeans of current and future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am sure Singaporeans will be excited to be able to buy a new flat in Tengah $140,000 under the AHS and live in it for their entire lives without having to pay land cost, instead of paying $350,000 under the current BTO scheme.

sections.label: Deferred land cost repayment
sections.summary: A Singaporean who buys a flat under AHS must repay deferred land cost with accrued interest upon sale, needing about $700,000 to profit after 25 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, to be fair to other Singaporeans, he will need to repay the deferred land cost with accrued interest to the Government upon the sale of his flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, whether a Singaporean buys a 4-room BTO flat in Tengah $350,000 or the same flat for $148,000 under AHS, he will need to sell it at about $700,000 in order to make a profit after 25 years.

sections.label: Resale flat grant increase
sections.summary: The Member welcomes the Government's move to increase the housing grant for first-timers buying a resale flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Chairman, I welcome, the Government's move to increase it the housing grant for first-timers buying a resale flat.

sections.label: Grant sizing and fiscal impact
sections.summary: The Member asks why the grant increase is $30,000 for a 4-room or smaller flat and $10,000 for a 5-room flat, and its estimated fiscal impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry also share further details about why the increase in grants is sized at $30,000 for a 4-room or smaller flat or $10,000 for a 5-room flat?

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: What is the estimated fiscal impact of this increase in grants?

sections.label: Itinerant shopfront traders and ODAs
sections.summary: Itinerant shopfront traders secure outdoor display area space from shop owners or lessees for a few hours daily, while HDB rules require shops to display the same trade items in their ODAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Over the last few years, an itinerant industry of shopfront traders have emerged, particularly in smaller commercial areas, moving from place to place and securing outdoor display areas or outdoor display areas (ODAs) space directly from shop owners or lessees for a few hours each day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The HDB Commercial department rules currently require that commercial shops are required to display the same trade items in their respective ODAs.

sections.label: Unfair competition accusations
sections.summary: Itinerant traders raise accusations of unfair competition among some HDB commercial and retail shop owners and lessees who follow the rules and display the same items in their ODAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the number of itinerant traders can be small and constantly varies, they do raise accusations of unfair competition amongst some HDB commercial and retail shop owners and lessees who: one, adhere to the rules and do not sublet their ODA; and two, display the same items in the ODAs as they do in their shops.

sections.label: Heartland Innovation and Transformation Programme
sections.summary: Market places can be conducive for new entrepreneurs to try startups or test-bed business ideas, and the Member is happy about the Heartland Innovation and Transformation Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: These market places can also be a conducive environment for new entrepreneurs who may wish to try out a small startup or to test-bed their business ideas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Hence, I am very happy to hear of the Heartland Innovation and Transformation Programme announced at the Ministry of Trade and Indutsry (MTI)'s COS this year.

sections.label: Revitalisation of Shops scheme
sections.summary: Asks whether MND will enhance the Revitalisation of Shops scheme to upgrade shops and inject vibrancy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Can I ask if MND will look into enhancing the Revitalisation of Shops (ROS) scheme to upgrade the shops and to inject new vibrancy?

sections.label: Hawker centre distribution statistics
sections.summary: Cites NEA figures of 118 hawker centres and notes uneven distribution across divisions and Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Some interesting statistics which I found, based on NEA’s list of hawker centres as at December, there are, currently, 118 hawker centres in Singapore, 27 directly managed by NEA, 80 by Town Councils (TCs), 10 by private operators and one is not in operation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It appears that, on the one hand, Jalan Besar and Tanjong Pagar have a disproportionately higher number of hawker centres per division while, on the other hand, Choa Chu Kang and Sengkang TCs do not have any hawker centres within their boundaries.

sections.label: NEA hawker centres in new estates
sections.summary: Says NEA-managed hawker centres should be central to new estate planning and built ahead of demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hawker centres directly managed by NEA should be central to the planning of new estates and built ahead of demand in new estates.

sections.label: Singles buying larger BTO flats
sections.summary: Notes singles can buy two-room flexi flats in non-mature estates and hopes they may buy 3-room and mature estate BTOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, singles can by two-room flexi flats in non‐mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will also allow singles to buy 3-room BTOs in non‐mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Indeed, if we could be even bolder, why not 2-room and 3-room BTOs for singles in mature estates, too, especially after the supply crunch abates?

sections.label: Rethink of BTO system
sections.summary: Recalls Leon Perera's idea and Desmond Lee's assurance on shorter waiting time flats, and calls for a fundamental rethink of BTO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: During the housing debate earlier this year, my hon friend Leon Perera mooted this idea as well, recognising that if we can build industrial facilities ahead of demand, can we not also build residential homes ahead of demand?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I do appreciate Minister Desmond Lee’s assurance that HDB is planning to launch more shorter waiting time flats of around 2,000 to 3,000 flats per year by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: However, this is, essentially, at similar levels to the number of such flats launched in the last five years, ranging from 1,096 in 2018 to 2,850 in 2020, representing a mere 7% to 18% of BTO supply in each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Beyond addressing the near-term demand-supply imbalance, I believe it is time for us to have a fundamental rethink of the BTO system.

sections.label: Hybrid approach supply resilience
sections.summary: Says the proposed hybrid approach's small risk of excess supply would strengthen HDB flat supply security against shocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Even if the hybrid approach I proposed entails a small risk of marginal excess supply, this would strengthen the security of supply of HDB flats, making us more resilient to potential supply-side shocks, as we have seen in the wake of COVID-19.

sections.label: Young entrepreneurs in Paya Lebar
sections.summary: Young entrepreneurs can be given spaces in localities to offer new products and services, with Paya Lebar Airbase development as a pilot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Young entrepreneurs can also be given spaces in these localities to offer new products and services, creating a space for social entrepreneurship and business incubation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We have the opportunity at the Paya Lebar Airbase development to pilot these models and a new way forward for Singapore's housing.

sections.label: HDB housing loan funds source
sections.summary: HDB housing loans are funded from the Development Fund, not CPF, with MOF providing funds at the CPF OA rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: As it turns out, the funds obtained by HDB to issue housing loans are from the Development Fund, not CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Consequently, it is MOF that provides these funds to HDB and sets them at the prevailing CPF OA rate.

sections.label: CPF Board bank interest rate
sections.summary: The CPF Board's assessment of major local banks' interest rate at 0.52% for November 2022 to January 2023 appears unrealistically low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: As I have raised in my cuts to MOM, the CPF Board’s assessment of the major local banks' interest rate to be at 0.52% for the period November 2022 to January 2023 appears unrealistically low, given the realities of the deposit environment of the local banks today, and does not reflect economic reality.

sections.label: HDB loan delinquency rate history
sections.summary: A question asks about the historical delinquency rate of loans to buy HDB flats over the last 30 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What is the historical delinquency rate of loans taken to buy HDB flats, with breakdown by loans from HDB and private financial institutions, for the last 30 years?

sections.label: Joint Singles Scheme pilot update
sections.summary: A question asks MND for an update on the JSS-OR pilot and whether it will expand to more sites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On public housing rental, can MND give an update on the Joint Singles Scheme-Operator Run (JSS-OR) pilot that was rolled out in end 2021 as an alternative option to the Joint Singles Scheme (JSS) for singles in public rental, and whether there are plans to expand the pilot to more sites?

sections.label: Public Rental Scheme eligibility and flats
sections.summary: Most applicants must have household incomes not more than $1,500 monthly, waiting time is about eight months, and flats are one-room and two-room.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Most applicants must have household incomes of not more than $1,500 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If one is approved, the waiting time for allocation of flats is about eight months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The sizes of the flats available under the Public Rental Scheme (PRS) are restricted to one-room flats and two-room flats.

sections.label: Rental flat income cut-off review
sections.summary: Asks whether HDB would review the household income cut-off for rental flats and expand the JSS-OR pilot to more sites.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, moving forward, would HDB consider reviewing the household income cut-off for rental flats, to say, $2,500 per month?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Does HDB plan to expand the JSS-OR pilot to more sites?

sections.label: Public Rental Scheme purpose
sections.summary: The Public Rental Scheme assists Singaporeans with no alternative housing options by providing heavily subsidised rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Public Rental Scheme (PRS) assists Singaporeans with no alternative housing options by providing them with heavily subsidised rental flats.

sections.label: JSS-OR demand and residential fires
sections.summary: Asks about demand and supply for JSS-OR and expansion plans, and notes 934 residential fires last year, about a third electrical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What is the demand and supply for JSS-OR and are there plans to expand this pilot to more sites?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: There were 934 cases of residential fires last year, of which about a third were of electrical origin.

sections.label: DfMA adoption in building projects
sections.summary: The Ministry shared that around 44% of building projects by gross floor area adopted DfMA in 2021, targeting 70% by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Ministry shared that around 44% of building projects by gross floor area adopted DfMA in 2021 and the target was to reach 70% by 2025.

sections.label: PIP support for DfMA and IDD
sections.summary: Under PIP, applicants can receive support of up to 70% of the cost of adopting solutions like DfMA and IDD technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Under PIP, applicants can benefit from support of up to 70% of the cost of adopting solutions like DfMA and IDD technologies.

sections.label: Repurposing under-utilised multi-storey car parks
sections.summary: In the 2021 COS debate, the speaker suggested under-utilised multi-storey car parks in many non-mature estates be partly repurposed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the 2021 COS debate, I suggested the multi-storey car parks (MSCPs) in many non-mature states are under-utilised and asked a part of them be repurposed.

sections.label: Tree pruning and rising costs
sections.summary: NParks advised Town Councils to prune trees more aggressively due to bird roosting, and rising costs may raise residents' Service and Conservancy Charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: When Town Councils prune trees, the idea is to preserve the natural shade that trees provide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, with the escalation of bird roosting in HDB estates, NParks have advised Town Councils to carry out more aggressive and regular pruning of trees than would ordinarily be the case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: There is one example of it in Bukit Batok.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Such roller shutters will have to be maintained every month, like lifts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: My concern is that all these escalating costs, if not defrayed by HDB, will have to be saddled by residents in form of increased Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC).

sections.label: Rising cooked food prices
sections.summary: Residents are concerned about rising cooked food prices, and MND is asked how it will keep heartland cooked meals affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Residents are understandably concerned about ever-rising prices of cooked food and price inflation in ingredients, electricity and gas have further pushed up prices of cook food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: How might MND ensure that cooked meals at eating houses in our heartlands remain affordable for Singaporeans?

sections.label: Anchorvale hawker food prices
sections.summary: Volunteer-gathered data suggest hawker food in Anchorvale is about 50 cents more expensive on average than in mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Data that my volunteer team and I had painstakingly gathered suggest that hawker food in Anchorvale, the division of Sengkang that I represent, is significantly more expensive compared to more mature estates by an average of around 50 cents.

sections.label: Bidding for HDB commercial spaces
sections.summary: Bidding for HDB commercial spaces, including coffee shops and hawker centre spaces, follows the standard price quality method.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The current bidding for HDB commercial spaces including coffee shops and hawker centre spaces follows the standard price quality method (PQM).

sections.label: Coffee shop bidding and prices
sections.summary: Open bidding for coffee shop spaces encourages high bids, passed on as higher rents and then higher consumer prices, as a $41-million Tampines bid shows.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Open bidding for coffee shop spaces encourages high bids, which is generally passed on to individual store owners through higher rents and subsequently to the end consumer via higher prices.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: As the $41-million winning bid for a Tampines coffee shop last year reminds us, such an escalation of bidding is a reality, as is the higher rents that result.

sections.label: Mitigating coffee shop bidding
sections.summary: Applying the same principles to coffee shop bids may mitigate first-price auction bidding and help keep coffee shop prices lower for residents.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Applying the self-same principles for coffee shop bids may help mitigate the race to the top or the bottom, depending on one's point of view, present in first-price auction bidding, and help keep coffee shop prices much lower for our residents.

sections.label: Resale flat supply measures
sections.summary: MND is asked whether it will consider measures to unlock resale supply, such as requiring owners who buy private property to sell their flats or banning renting out HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Will MND consider further measures to unlock the resale supply in the resale market, such as requiring HDB owners who buy private property to sell their flats, or to ban them from renting their HDB flats?

sections.label: Silver Housing Bonus applications
sections.summary: The Minister is asked for an update on how many seniors have applied for the Silver Housing Bonus and the Lease Buyback Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update on how many seniors have applied for the Silver Housing Bonus and the Lease Buyback Scheme respectively?

sections.label: Eldercare demand by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, almost one in three people in Singapore will need some form of eldercare service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By 2030, almost one in three people in Singapore will need some form of eldercare service.

sections.label: Nursing home bed occupancy
sections.summary: High demand for nursing homes has led to bed occupancy rates exceeding 90%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The high demand for nursing homes has led to bed occupancy rates exceeding 90%.

sections.label: More CCAs after oversubscription
sections.summary: Given that both launches were over-subscribed, it is asked whether there are plans for more CCAs to be built.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Given that both launches were over-subscribed, are there plans for more CCAs to be built?

sections.label: EASE programme and seniors
sections.summary: The EASE programme is said to have made public housing flats more elderly-friendly, and updates are sought on lower-income seniors benefiting and on expanding supportable items.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Since its introduction in 2012, the EASE programme has been instrumental in making our public housing flats more elderly-friendly for our senior residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I welcome the $295 million top-up to the HIP and EASE programme as announced in Budget 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am also encouraged that 1-, 2- and 3- room flat residents can receive subsidies of up to 95% for EASE programme upgrading works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is crucial that seniors in the lower-income strata be able to comfortably age-in-place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to seek updates on how many lower-income seniors or seniors living 1- and 2- room flats have benefited from the EASE programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Also, is the Ministry considering an expansion of supportable items, such as features that are in CCAs?

sections.label: Seniors using Silver Housing Bonus
sections.summary: MND is asked to update on the number of seniors who chose to right-size and got the Silver Housing Bonus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Could MND update on the number of seniors who have chosen to right-size and successfully got the Silver Housing Bonus?

sections.label: HDB blocks without lift access
sections.summary: An update is sought on HDB blocks with incomplete lift access, last reported as about 150, and the 2020 lift access housing grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: First of all, I would like to see an update on the current number of HDB blocks in Singapore with incomplete lift access for all flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We were last told that there were about 150 such HDB blocks in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: At COS 2021, the Minister said that the lift access housing grant of up to $30,000 was introduced in 2020 to assist residents with urgent mobility or medical needs to move to another flat with direct lift access.

sections.label: Maintenance plans for ageing estates
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked about maintenance plans for ageing estates like Henderson Crescent, including HIP, SERS or VERS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry share and update on its maintenance plans for ageing estates, like Henderson Crescent, including the Home Improvement Programme scheme or can HDB consider SERS for the flats at Henderson Crescent?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If there are no plans for SERS, can the Ministry provide some information on VERS?

sections.label: Lift access for segmental blocks
sections.summary: HDB is asked whether owners in the remaining 150 segmental blocks can sell flats back at market prices with the Lift access Housing Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The corner odd-floor units of these two blocks would have direct access to the lift on the same level, if more than 75% of the residents support the LUP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: I understand from HDB that the cost of providing lift for the remaining 150 segmental blocks may cost $200,000 per household.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: For such segmented units, can HDB provide an option for the owners to sell their flat back to HDB at market prices, while enjoying the Lift access Housing Grant or LHG.

sections.label: HIP extension to 1987-1997 flats
sections.summary: In 2018, the HIP was extended to flats built between 1987 and 1997.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2018, the HIP was extended to flats built between 1987 and 1997.

sections.label: NParks complaints and enforcement
sections.summary: NParks receives about 1,200 complaints yearly, with about 20 warning letters, 38 fines and six jail cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: NParks receives about 1,200 complaints on average each year, of which about 20 result in warning letters, 38 in fines and six in jail.

sections.label: Maximum ban for owners
sections.summary: Some members of the public say the maximum 12-month ban for owners is lenient and courts seldom impose upper jail limits of up to three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some members of the public have pointed out that the maximum ban of 12 months for owners is lenient and it appears that the Courts do not often impose upper limits of jail terms, which go up to three years.

sections.label: Town Council bird reports
sections.summary: Since February 2022, the Town Council has received more than a thousand reports about birds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Since February 2022, the Town Council has received more than a thousand reports about birds.

sections.label: Thomson Sin Ming Court chickens
sections.summary: Free-roaming chickens at Thomson Sin Ming Court multiplied, so a task force of residents with NParks, Town Council and Acres support was set up; about 60 chickens remain, down from around 100 in December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Wild, free roaming chickens have multiplied so fast at one of my estates, Thomson Sin Ming Court, that a task force comprising mainly residents, with representatives from NParks, Town Council and Acres in support, was set up to attend to the feedback from two groups of residents with opposing views.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: At last count, we had about 60 chickens, down from around 100 in December 2021, after a few exercises to relocate some.

sections.label: Fight over chicken feeding
sections.summary: A fight broke out between residents due to chicken feeding and a police report was lodged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Recently, a fight even broke out between residents due to chicken feeding and a police report was lodged.

sections.label: NParks engaging chicken feeders
sections.summary: NParks will engage the feeders but there is no deterrence as feeding of chickens is not an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: NParks will engage the feeders but there is no deterrence as feeding of chickens is not an offence.

sections.label: Public consultation on cats
sections.summary: The speaker is glad a public consultation was done and hopes the Minister will update progress and share brief conditions being considered to allow keeping cats in HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I am glad we have finally done a public consultation on this issue and it seems we are moving forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I hope Minister can provide a further update on the progress on this issue and share some of the brief conditions the Ministry is considering imposing to allow the keeping of cats in HDB flats.

sections.label: Animal abuse penalties review
sections.summary: Calls to increase penalties and disqualification periods for animal abuse, and to emphasise Mandatory Treatment Order, with a review update sought.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: There is also growing awareness and concerns about animal welfare and rightly so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: It is time for us to increase the penalties for animal abuse and cruelty and also increase the length of time offenders can be disqualified from owning animals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: We should also emphasise the role of Mandatory Treatment Order as a sentencing option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I understand the Ministry is reviewing this and I hope Minister can provide an update and timeline for this review.

sections.label: New Single Singles Scheme
sections.summary: Proposes that HDB consider a new Single Singles Scheme in addition to the Joint Singles Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Everyone has their own habits, lifestyles and sharing a common living space with a stranger is really not easy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to propose that HDB consider a new Single Singles Scheme in addition to the Joint Singles Scheme.

sections.label: Joint Singles Scheme pilot update
sections.summary: Asks MND for an update on the Joint Singles Scheme Operator-run pilot rolled out in end 2021 for singles in public rental.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Can MND give an update on the Joint Singles Scheme Operator-run (JSS-OR) pilot which was rolled out in end 2021 as an alternative option to the JSS for singles in public rental.

sections.label: Divorce housing information asymmetry
sections.summary: Suggests resolving information asymmetry between Courts, HDB and divorcing couples on housing arrangements for young children post-divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: First, in cases of divorce involving young children, there may be a case to resolve the information asymmetry between the Courts, HDB and the divorcing couples on the issue of ensuring proper housing arrangements for their young children post-divorce.

sections.label: Overcrowding in rental flats
sections.summary: States the Government must decisively tackle overcrowding in rental flats that inhibits children's ability to grow up well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Next, this Government must decisively tackle overcrowding in rental flats that inhibit the ability of our children in these households to grow up well.

sections.label: Seniors selling flats to children
sections.summary: Suggests the Minister look into seniors who sell their flats to fund children's, relatives' or friends' flat purchases but are later turfed out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Separately, I suggest that the hon Minister look into the plight of seniors who sell their flats to help fund the purchase of flats belonging to their children, relatives or friends but only to be turfed out later.

sections.label: Differentiated LTV for first-time owners
sections.summary: The passage states that saving extra cash for a downpayment may set first-time home owners further back, and calls for a differentiated LTV for them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The need to save for the additional cash for downpayment may set them further back on their home ownership journey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to have a differentiated LTV for first-time home owners as it exists in some other countries.

sections.label: HDB policy for divorcing couples
sections.summary: The passage asks whether HDB can review its policy to let a divorcing couple buy a replacement flat pending finalisation of the divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: Can HDB review its policy so as to allow a divorcing couple to buy a replacement flat pending finalisation of the divorce?

sections.label: First-timer BTO success rates
sections.summary: MND shared that 90% of first-timers succeed within two tries for a non-mature estate BTO and virtually all within three tries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: MND has shared that, as it stands now, 90% of all first-timers succeed within two tries for a BTO in the non-mature estate and virtually all succeed within three tries.

sections.label: Fresh Start 3-room flat option
sections.summary: MND announced grant enhancements and scheme expansion to 3-room flats, and clarified that Fresh Start applicants can now have the 3-room flat option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: In last year's Committee of Supply (COS), MND announced enhancements to the grant amount as well as an expansion of the scheme to offer the option of 3-room flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: MND said it is working on the on the implementation for the offer of a 3-room flat under Fresh Start and will announce the details when ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: I note that in the latest BTO exercise just launched, MND has clarified that now Fresh Start applicants can have the 3-room flat option available.

sections.label: Fresh Start enhancements and outreach
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government is considering further enhancements to the Fresh Start Housing scheme and how outreach can be widened.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Is the Government considering further enhancements to the Fresh Start Housing scheme and how can outreach be widened?

sections.label: Revitalising Kampong Glam
sections.summary: The passage suggests considering revitalising Kampong Glam and linking it as an extension of the vibrant Bugis area.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: An example of such a place is Kampong Glam.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: We can consider revitalising Kampong Glam and link that as an extension of the vibrant Bugis area.

sections.label: Long-Term Plan Review Phase 4 findings
sections.summary: MND is asked for an update on Phase 4 of the Long-Term Plan Review and which public consultation feedback will feature in land use plans.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: With Phase 4 of LTPR concluding, can MND provide an update on the key findings and what aspects of the public consultation feedback will feature in our land use plans?

sections.label: Green spaces and ground-up planning
sections.summary: The passage asks whether public interest in green spaces and sustainability will evolve into ground-up planning of facilities with residents.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: In 2021, $25 billion has been planned for our nation’s research, innovation and enterprise development landscape, with urban solutions and sustainability being a key research domain.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: URA’s Long-Term Plan Review in 2022 saw many participants from the public express interest in having green spaces and sustainability concepts being incorporated in our future land use masterplan.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: To take this beyond just community gardens that we have today, will it evolve to having ground-up planning of facilities creation with residents and better use of spaces for functional purpose that fits the local demographics, instead of just generic exercise corners or playgrounds?

sections.label: Marine EIA transparency online
sections.summary: The passage states that the EIA framework was changed to enhance transparency, but several recent marine EIAs were not made available online.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2022, the Government announced the important changes to Singapore’s Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) framework which includes enhancing the transparency of such environmental studies.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, a number of recent marine EIAs were not made available online.

sections.label: Future marine EIAs online
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government plans to make future marine EIAs available online, with redaction of confidential portions if necessary.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Government share whether it plans to make future marine EIAs available online, perhaps with redaction of confidential portions, if necessary?

sections.label: Long-Term Plan Review concluded
sections.summary: The passage states that last year MND and URA concluded the Long-Term Plan Review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, last year, MND and URA concluded the Long-Term Plan Review.

sections.label: Building energy audit requirement study
sections.summary: The passage states that MND announced it was exploring whether to require building owners to conduct energy audits to improve energy performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MND announced earlier that it was exploring whether to require building owners to conduct energy audits to improve the energy performance of their buildings.

sections.label: Development and conservation principles
sections.summary: Asks what principles URA uses to decide on development and conservation and whether a task force coordinates agencies for science-based sustainable development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Furthermore, situations may arise when building new human-centric recreational activities requires careful scrutiny and planning to avoid destroying habitats, such as proposals to clear parts of the Springleaf Forest for Nee Soon Park or to increase traffic to our Southern Islands to create tourism opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: In these delicate situations, what principles does the URA use to decide on development and conservation and is there a dedicated task force to coordinate the plans of different agencies to ensure that we take a science-based approach and ensure sustainable development?

sections.label: OneMillionTrees Movement planting target
sections.summary: Under the OneMillionTrees Movement, Singapore aims to plant a million more trees by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Under the OneMillionTrees Movement, we aim to plant a million more trees across Singapore by 2030.

sections.label: NParks species recovery plans
sections.summary: NParks aims to carry out recovery plans for over 70 more animal and plant species by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: NParks also aims to carry out recovery plans for over 70 more animal and plant species by 2030.

sections.label: ACS Primary relocation to Tengah
sections.summary: The relocation of ACS Primary School to Tengah will likely increase desirability of BTOs there and improve school accessibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The recent announcement of the relocation of ACS Primary School to Tengah will likely increase the desirability of BTOs in Tengah estate as well as improve accessibility of the school.

sections.label: Surveys on work-from-home productivity
sections.summary: Many surveys point to increased productivity when people work from home, including a Prodoscore report of a 47% rise since March 2020 in the US.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Contrary to what many expected, many surveys point to an increase in productivity when people work from home, including one by Prodoscore, a productivity intelligence company that reports that there was an increase in productivity by 47% since March 2020, compared to the same period in the previous year in the US.

sections.label: Permaculture education national effort
sections.summary: Proposes that MND make permaculture education a national effort to engage citizens in action for people's and the planet's wellness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: To engage our citizens constructively in action for our people’s and the planet’s wellness, I propose MND to make permaculture education a national effort.

sections.label: Permaculture gardens in HDB estates
sections.summary: Speaker learned of permaculture from Catherine Loke, who proposes community-maintained permaculture gardens on unused HDB and park land.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I got to know about permaculture from Ms Catherine Loke, the Founding President of The Circle for Human Sustainability – a collective in Singapore made of architects, engineers, sociologists, scientists, design leaders and farmers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: She has a visionary idea of Little Farms Everywhere for Singapore, to utilise the currently unused plots of land between our HDB blocks and in our community parks for permaculture gardens, maintained by the community, for the community.

sections.label: Permaculture and Singapore food imports
sections.summary: Scaling permaculture would lessen food supply chain issues for Singapore, which imports more than 90% of its food.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: If permaculture is implemented at scale, food supply chain issues would be less of an issue as it is now for Singapore, because we now import more than 90% of our food.

sections.label: Cuba's permaculture recovery and Singapore
sections.summary: Cuba used permaculture in 1990s reforms, recovering agricultural production; speaker urges MND to support permaculture and land use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: It was plunged into a severe economic and food crisis in the 1990s when the Soviet Union dissolved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: But within a decade, it recovered sufficiently to double agricultural production, increase calorific availability by 25% for its people and maintain a consistent and equitable social food programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Permaculture methods featured strongly in the reforms of Cuba at that time, and it is worth further studying to see what good practices we can adopt to ensure Singapore’s food resilience and future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I urge MND to avail more land towards regenerative nature technology research, including utilising current unused pockets of land in our HDB estates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: We can work with interested Singaporeans to make permaculture part of the Singaporean way of life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: All MND needs to do is to allow and to support them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: We can even transform the current “illegal planting” problem plaguing many HDB estates into little farms that empower and engage our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Of course, this requires hard work and effort, especially in finding solutions to disamenities, like rooster crowing too early, disturbing residents.

sections.label: Poor mental health survey findings
sections.summary: The National Population Health Survey 2020 reported 13.4% of the population had poor mental health, with ages 18 to 29 highest at 21.5%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The National Population Health Survey 2020 reported 13.4% of the population having poor mental health, of which younger adults aged 18 to 29 made up the highest proportion at 21.5%.

sections.label: MND support for shared community spaces
sections.summary: The question asks how MND can support community stakeholders in older estates to co-create shared spaces promoting mental well-being and inclusivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: How can MND support such efforts in older estates amongst community stakeholders to reimagine and co-create shared spaces in the community to promote residents’ mental well-being and inclusivity?

sections.label: Buildings' share of carbon emissions
sections.summary: Buildings account for over 20% of Singapore's carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Chairman, buildings account for over 20% of Singapore's carbon emissions.

sections.label: low-carbon built environment transition
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government is accelerating the transition to a low-carbon built environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: How is the Government accelerating our transition to a low‐carbon built environment?

sections.label: greening older buildings and jobs
sections.summary: The passage asks what more can be done to green older, less energy efficient buildings and what job opportunities Singaporeans can look forward to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Specifically, what more can be done to green our existing stock of older and less energy efficient buildings and what exciting job opportunities can Singaporeans look forward to as we continue to push for greener buildings?

sections.label: contractor payment and Variation Orders
sections.summary: The passage states contractors must be paid timely and that Variation Orders are not certified or paid in full until project completion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, contractors must be paid in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Variation Orders (VOs) are also not certified or paid in full, until the project is completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some VOs for larger projects can amount to millions of dollars, severely affecting contractors’ cash flow, without timely payments from clients.

sections.label: contractors waiting for TOP
sections.summary: The passage states contractors often experience long waits for Temporary Occupation Permits from various Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Contractors often experience long waits for Temporary Occupation Permits (TOP) from the various Government agencies.

sections.label: buildings carbon emissions and MND
sections.summary: The passage states buildings account for over 20% of Singapore's carbon emissions and asks about MND's plan to expedite the transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Chairman, buildings in Singapore account for over 20% of our carbon emissions, what are MND’s plan to expedite our transition to a low-carbon built environment?

sections.label: neighbourhood noise quiet hours enforcement
sections.summary: The passage asks how the extended quiet hours from the Community Advisory Panel on neighbourhood noise are being enforced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: Chairman, last year, Municipal Services Office (MSO) set up a Community Advisory Panel (CAP) on neighbourhood noise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: I have several queries: first, how are the extended quiet hours being enforced?

sections.label: Extended quiet hours success measures
sections.summary: Asks what measures determine the success of extended quiet hours and whether MND will legislate if violations continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: Second, what measures are being used to determine the success of the extended quiet hours?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: If this does not resolve the conflicts, and perpetuators continue to violate the guidelines, will MND move legislation to resolve the problem?

sections.label: Community wardens pilot programme
sections.summary: In 2015, citizens were appointed as community wardens in a pilot programme to support Police responding to noise complaints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: In 2015, citizens were appointed as community wardens, as a pilot programme to support the Police to respond to noise complaints.

sections.label: Housing market stability and BTO outcomes
sections.summary: Housing market was stable until COVID-19 disrupted building; supply was ramped up and BTO prices kept almost flat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The housing market had been stable for a number of years until COVID-19 severely disrupted our building programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We responded decisively to stabilise the situation and catch up on lost time, ramped up supply significantly and kept BTO prices almost flat in the last two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Therefore, even in 2022, virtually all first-timers who applied for BTO flats in non-mature estates were successful within three tries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And more than eight in 10 BTO and resale flat buyers could service their HDB loans using their CPF contributions, with little to no cash outlay.

sections.label: Greatearth BTO projects completion
sections.summary: Three former Greatearth BTO projects were completed, two ahead of schedule, with 20,000 more flats due this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have since completed three of the former Greatearth BTO projects and delivered two of them ahead of their estimated completion dates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This year, we are on track to complete and hand over keys to another 20,000 HDB flats across 22 housing projects.

sections.label: 100,000 new flats launch
sections.summary: Up to 100,000 new flats will be launched in total from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As I have said before, we will launch up to 100,000 new flats in total from 2021 to 2025.

sections.label: First-Timer Parents and Married Couples category
sections.summary: A new category, First-Timer (Parents and Married Couples), will give enhanced support when applying for a new HDB flat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These young married couples and parents also probably have shorter work experience, so they might not have sufficient savings to afford other housing options at the time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, we will introduce a new category: First-Timer (Parents and Married Couples), who will enjoy enhanced support when they apply for a new HDB flat.

sections.label: First-timer parents extra ballot
sections.summary: First-timer parents and married couples get one additional ballot when applying for a new HDB flat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In total, about 10% of all first-timer families will be considered first-timer parents and married couples for this sub-category.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, as Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong had announced during his Budget speech, first-timer parents and married couples will get one additional ballot when they apply for a new HDB flat.

sections.label: Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme
sections.summary: The scheme is renamed and flat supply set aside for families rises to up to 40% of BTO and 60% of SBF flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To reflect this expansion, we will rename it as the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And with more families qualifying, we will further increase the flat supply that we set aside for them – up to 40% of the BTO flat supply and 60% of the Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) flat supply, in all launches in mature estates, non-mature estates and prime location housing.

sections.label: Tighter non-selection rules
sections.summary: First-timers become second-timers for a year after one non-selection count, and second-timers sit out a year after one count.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: After careful consideration, we have decided for now to tighten the rules for non-selection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will consider first-timers as second-timers for a year when they ballot for a flat, after they receive one non-selection count, down from the two counts today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Similarly, second-timers will not be allowed to participate in HDB sales exercises for one year, after they receive one non-selection count.

sections.label: Non-selection count thresholds
sections.summary: HDB will not issue a non-selection count if BTO applicants have 10 or fewer flats left, or five for SBF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We want to be fair to applicants who have very limited options, when they are invited to select their flat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Therefore, HDB will not issue a non-selection count if BTO flat applicants have 10 or fewer flats left to choose from.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For Sale of Balanced Flat (SBF) exercises, where the flat supply is much smaller to begin with, we will use a lower threshold of five flats.

sections.label: August BTO exercise start
sections.summary: The announced moves take effect from this year's August BTO exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The moves that I have just announced will take effect from this year's August BTO exercise.

sections.label: CPF Housing Grant increase
sections.summary: A considered decision was made to increase the CPF Housing Grant and give targeted support to eligible first-timers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: With these in mind, we made a considered decision to increase the CPF Housing Grant and give targeted support to eligible first-timers, who made up about one-third of all resale flat buyers in the past two years.

sections.label: Increased CPF Housing Grant for singles
sections.summary: Eligible first-timer singles can receive increased CPF Housing Grants for resale flats, with Ms Yeo receiving $40,000 for her 3-room flat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Eligible first-timer singles can also enjoy the recently increased CPF Housing Grant announced during Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have increased it from $25,000 to $40,000 for singles buying 2- to 4-room resale flats and from $20,000 to $25,000 for 5-room resale flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Ms Yeo recently bought a 3-room resale flat in Serangoon and will receive the increased CPF Housing Grant of $40,000.

sections.label: Third Community Care Apartment project
sections.summary: A third Community Care Apartment project will be launched in Bedok later this year for seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We also received valuable feedback from seniors, who were keen to apply and who wanted us to build more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, I am happy to announce that we will launch a third Community Care Apartment project in Bedok later this year, for our seniors.

sections.label: BTO flat affordability example
sections.summary: A household earning $2,500 can receive $70,000 in grants, reducing a Jurong West 3-room flat to $150,000 with zero cash outlay.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For example, in the ongoing BTO exercise, the typical selling price for a 3-room flat in Jurong West Crystal is $220,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: A household with a monthly income of $2,500 can receive $70,000 in housing grants, which will further reduce the price of the flat to $150,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This household will need to use about 19% of their monthly income to pay for their mortgage instalments, which means that they can service their mortgage fully using their monthly CPF contributions, with zero cash outlay.

sections.label: 1990s property boom queue
sections.summary: During the mid-1990s property boom, up to 150,000 flat buyers queued and waits could last seven years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: At the height of the property boom in the mid-1990s, there were as many as 150,000 flat buyers in the queue, and the wait for a flat could be as long as seven years.

sections.label: 2022 CPF loan servicing
sections.summary: In 2022, more than eight in 10 BTO and resale flat buyers could service HDB loans using CPF with little to no cash.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Overall, in 2022, more than eight in 10 BTO and resale flat buyers could service their HDB loans using their CPF contributions, with little to no cash outlay.

sections.label: HDB loan limits and arrears
sections.summary: Arrears among HDB loan households stayed stable, and the loan-to-value limit was lowered in September to encourage financial prudence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The proportion of households in arrears amongst those servicing HDB loans has also remained fairly stable over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: On raising the loan-to-value limit for first-timers, as Ms Foo Mee Har had suggested, we appreciate her intent to make flats more affordable for them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We recently lowered the limit for HDB housing loans in September last year to encourage flat buyers, including first-timers, to exercise more financial prudence, especially in a rising interest rate environment and an environment of greater economic uncertainty.

sections.label: Additional BTO ballot chance
sections.summary: First-Timer Parents and Married Couples get an additional ballot when applying for a BTO flat in any estate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, First-Timer Parents and Married Couples will get an additional ballot when they apply for a BTO flat in any estate.

sections.label: Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme
sections.summary: First-timer married couples qualify for the scheme, 40% of 3-room or larger BTO flats set aside, first priority given, and CPF Housing Grant enhanced to $80,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Apart from first-timer families with children, first-timer married couples will also qualify for the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And we will increase the proportion of the 3-room or larger BTO flat supply set aside for eligible applicants to 40%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Third, under the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme, First-Timer Parents and Married Couples will enjoy first priority, so they will stand a higher chance of being invited to select a flat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We also recently enhanced the CPF Housing Grant to a maximum amount of $80,000, to support first-timers who want to buy a resale flat instead.

sections.label: Upcoming HDB projects and homes
sections.summary: Mount Pleasant, Keppel Club and Bayshore projects will yield about 17,000 HDB flats, and Greater Southern Waterfront and Paya Lebar Airbase will offer some 150,000 homes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Singaporeans can look forward to upcoming projects at Mount Pleasant, Keppel Club and Bayshore, which will yield about 17,000 HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And further down the road in the 2030s and 2040s, we will open up the Greater Southern Waterfront for urban living and redevelop the Paya Lebar Airbase area to offer some 150,000 public and private homes.

sections.label: Long-Term Plan Review launch
sections.summary: In mid-2021, MND and URA launched the Long-Term Plan Review mapping land use strategies for the next 50 years and beyond.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In mid-2021, MND and the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) launched the Long-Term Plan Review, which mapped out our land use strategies to guide Singapore's development for the next 50 years and beyond.

sections.label: URA engagement with people
sections.summary: URA had engaged over 15,000 people from all walks of life.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Since then, URA had engaged over 15,000 people from all walks of life.

sections.label: Heritage conservation and Identity Corridors
sections.summary: Over 7,200 heritage buildings and structures were conserved in 30 years, and Identity Corridors will enhance historic trunk roads like the Historic East corridor.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In the last 30 years, over 7,200 heritage buildings and structures have been conserved.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Beyond individual buildings, we also enhance familiar neighbourhoods and shape new places to make them memorable.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will reinforce this through Identity Corridors, where we will use urban and streetscape design to enhance the character of historic trunk roads, such as the Historic East corridor that cuts across Joo Chiat and Geylang Serai.

sections.label: Flexible plans for Greater Southern Waterfront
sections.summary: Plans for areas such as the Greater Southern Waterfront are intentionally kept flexible and their development paced out.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For example, in developing plans for areas, such as the Greater Southern Waterfront, we intentionally keep our plans flexible and pace out their development.

sections.label: Masterplan Review and public engagement
sections.summary: The Masterplan Review will give effect to strategies over 10 to 15 years, with detailed land use plans and engagement avenues over two to three years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: However, in order to get there, we will have to start giving effect to these strategies and plans over the next 10 to 15 years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This exercise is known as the Masterplan Review and it will provide detailed land use and development plans covering sites all over Singapore, from major transformation areas, such as the Greater Southern Waterfront and Paya Lebar Airbase, to residential towns, neighbourhoods and our heartlands.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As highlighted by Ms Nadia Samdin, we will provide various avenues to engage Singaporeans of all ages and from all walks of life, to share their views on our national and local plans.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This will be done over the next two to three years.

sections.label: Dual bicycle racks in HDB towns
sections.summary: HDB plans to install 40,000 dual bicycle racks in 23 existing HDB towns by 2025 to optimise void deck space.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To optimise space at void decks, HDB also plans to install 40,000 dual bicycle racks, which can each hold two bicycles in 23 existing HDB towns by 2025.

sections.label: Community green spaces and rooftop urban farms
sections.summary: NParks' initiatives encourage community involvement in green spaces, while HDB and SFA's urban farms at 14 multi-storey car park rooftops contribute to food security.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: NParks' initiatives' such as Friends of the Parks and the Community in Bloom movement also encourage the local community to play a part in designing, developing and managing green spaces, while HDB and SFA's urban farms at 14 multi-storey car park rooftops contribute to food security.

sections.label: Marine Nature Areas and Marine Parks
sections.summary: Marine Nature Areas and Marine Parks at the Southern Islands are safeguarded in URA's Parks and Waterbodies Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For instance, we have safeguarded Marine Nature Areas and Marine Parks at our Southern Islands in URA's Parks and Waterbodies Plan.

sections.label: Upgrading flats above 30 years
sections.summary: Flats above 30 years have undergone MUP or will be selected for HIP by 2030, with next upgrading around 60 to 70 years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: All flats above 30 years would have already undergone the Main Upgrading Programme (MUP) in the past or will be selected for the Home Improvement Programme (HIP) by 2030 subject to the Government's fiscal position.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The next round of upgrading for these flats would be around 60 to 70 years of age.

sections.label: SERS eligible sites
sections.summary: Most projects with high redevelopment potential have been selected for SERS, and few more sites are expected to be eligible.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On Ms Joan Pereira's question about the Selective En bloc Redevelopment Scheme, or SERS, we shared that most projects with high redevelopment potential have already been selected for SERS and we do not expect many more sites to be eligible.

sections.label: HDB blocks without lift access
sections.summary: As of January 2023, about 140 HDB blocks have units without direct access to lifts on the same floor.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As of January 2023, there are only about 140 HDB blocks with units without direct access to lifts on the same floor.

sections.label: Lift access Housing Grant
sections.summary: The Lift access Housing Grant provides up to $30,000 to help residents buy another flat with lift access.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Dennis Tan has asked about the Lift access Housing Grant (LHG) which provides up to $30,000 to help residents buy another flat with lift access.

sections.label: HDB flat insurance premiums
sections.summary: An HDB-appointed company provides basic coverage, with flat owner premiums ranging between $1.63 and $8.18 for five-year coverage.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: An HDB-appointed company provides basic coverage and the premiums payable by flat owners range between $1.63 and $8.18 only, for a five-year coverage.

sections.label: Therapeutic Gardens
sections.summary: There are currently 10 Therapeutic Gardens, including three launched over the past year, and 20 more will be added by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For example, we currently have 10 Therapeutic Gardens, which are specially designed to improve the physical and mental well-being of people across a diverse range of physical abilities and health conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This includes three that we launched over the past year, and we will add 20 more by 2030.

sections.label: Trees in industrial estates
sections.summary: Since 2020, the number of trees in industrial estates has more than doubled, from 90,000 to 180,000 today.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Since 2020, we have more than doubled the number of trees in our industrial estates, from 90,000 to 180,000 today.

sections.label: Native species recovery target
sections.summary: Singapore has crossed the three-quarter mark of its 2030 species recovery target, covering 82 plant and 42 animal species.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This brings me to our efforts to conserve our native plant and animal species, which Ms Nadia Samdin asked about.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have crossed the three-quarter mark of our 2030 species recovery target, with 82 plant and 42 animal species covered today.

sections.label: Restoring 80 hectares habitats
sections.summary: Singapore aims to restore 80 hectares of forest, coastal and marine habitats by 2030 by planting native species and encouraging native animal populations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To provide more conducive habitats for our native biodiversity to thrive, we will raise our ambitions on this front.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We now aim to restore 80 hectares of forest, coastal, and marine habitats by 2030, by intensifying the planting of native species and encouraging the establishment of native animal populations.

sections.label: Community stewards and volunteers
sections.summary: Ideas included community stewards organising biodiversity surveys and curating educational resources, and growing over 60,000 volunteers and 11,000 citizen scientists.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This included ideas for community stewards to organise nature-based activities, such as biodiversity surveys, and to curate educational resources on the benefits of City in Nature through experiential learning.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will continue to grow our base of over 60,000 volunteers and over 11,000 citizen scientists.

sections.label: RIE 2025 research funding
sections.summary: Under the RIE 2025 Plan, close to $270 million is set aside for research on challenges such as climate change, including marine and blue carbon programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan, we have set aside close to $270 million for research to address new challenges in areas such as climate change.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: One of the research programmes funded under RIE 2025 is the Marine Climate Change Science programme, for which we have started to award grants.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Another looks at building up the foundational science for blue carbon accounting in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We also recently launched the first grant call under the City in Nature research vertical of the Cities of Tomorrow programme.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These research projects will help us deepen our scientific foundations and develop evidence-based management practices.

sections.label: Consultation on heartland shops
sections.summary: In 2021, MND and MTI consulted over 2,800 stakeholders over 11 months on transforming heartland shops, obtaining suggestions from residents and shop operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This is why, in 2021, MND and MTI jointly embarked on an extensive consultation exercise on this subject.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We engaged over 2,800 stakeholders over a 11-month period and obtained many valuable suggestions from residents and heartland shop operators on how these shops can be transformed.

sections.label: Enhanced Entrepreneur Scheme for startups
sections.summary: HDB sets aside up to 5% of new shops for innovative businesses, and the Enhanced Entrepreneur Scheme will allocate more spaces with a 10% rental discount.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Since 2018, HDB has been setting aside up to 5% of its new shops for direct allocation to startups or existing businesses with innovative business models.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will be launching the Enhanced Entrepreneur Scheme, in partnership with MTI and Enterprise SG, to allocate more shop spaces to eligible startups, and provide a 10% rental discount for their first three years.

sections.label: Heartland shop upgrading support
sections.summary: Threshold for upgrading relaxed to 75%, shop owners' co-payment cut from 20% to 5%, HDB share raised to 85%, and HDB co-funds 80% of optional shop-front works up to $3,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In January, we announced in Parliament that we would relax the threshold needed for upgrading to proceed, from 100% agreement amongst shop owners to 75%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We recognise, through feedback given to us by many local merchant associations, that shop owners may still be hesitant to undertake upgrading works, especially in the face of economic uncertainty and rising costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Therefore, to better assist our heartland shops, we will reduce the shop owners' co-payment share for ROS upgrading costs from 20% down to 5% and increase HDB's share from 70% to 85%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: HDB will also co-fund 80% of the costs for optional works at the shop front, for example, installing vertical blinds or roller shutters, up to a cap of $3,000.

sections.label: Support for inclusive enterprises
sections.summary: Rental discount for social enterprises and SG Enable-supported shops rises from 20% to 30% for three-year terms, renewable, and operators employing seniors aged 65 and above get extra PQM points.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: HDB has been supporting social enterprises and SG Enable-supported shops with inclusive hiring practices, by directly allocating them shop spaces and providing SMEs with a 20% rental discount for the first three-years.
